candidate.name: constraint_ledger
candidate.hypothesis: Most baseline failures are unverified constraints (18 bought without clicking a required offered option, 5 bought over budget, 5 substituted an absent value); injecting a per-turn derived constraint ledger will lift the 50-task train pass rate from 12/50 (0.24) to >=19/50 without harming the 12 passing episodes.
candidate.changes: transform_request only: parse the public instruction (budget bound, explicit size/color/quantity values with generic lexicons and number-word normalization), parse the current page (Price, clickables via ast.literal_eval, attribute-value grouping), track page-local clicked values from assistant tool_calls with page-change resets, then append a compact '[Constraint check]' block (~54 tokens) to the last observation stating budget OK/OVER, each requested value with the exact offered string to click or 'NOT offered -> click Back to Search', and a buy gate. transform_response stays identity; all logic is stateless per call, stdlib re/ast/copy/json only.
candidate.expected_efficiency: +~54 tokens per call (~8-12% total tokens), +1-2 turns only on converted episodes, no extra model calls; offline replay shows 0 false vetoes at buy turns on the 12 passing episodes and correct flags on 27/38 failures (remaining 8 are wrong-product-title failures not targeted by this mechanism).

candidate.name: progress_guard
candidate.hypothesis: Retaining the incumbent constraint ledger verbatim and appending a '[Progress check]' block only when the model's latest action re-clicks an already-clicked product id or navigation value will convert at least 2 of the 6 turn-cap loop failures (251,329,425,465,680,827), leave all 19 current passes unaffected because the guard is provably silent on every pass turn, and lift the 50-task train pass rate from 19/50 (0.38) to >=21/50 while cutting >=100K tokens from the 604K burned by those loops.
candidate.changes: New file agents/progress_guard.py = agents/constraint_ledger.py copied verbatim (all instruction/page parsing, value matching, ledger rendering, transform_request flow) plus one addition: a stateless repetition-triggered progress block. _click_trace(messages) collects every click_action value in message order; the block fires only when the most recent tool call is a click_action whose value is product-id-like (incumbent _PROD_ID_RE) or a nav control ('back to search', 'next >', '< prev') and has occurred at least twice overall (never on first occurrence, never on repeated search keywords, never on option re-clicks). When fired it appends 4 short lines after the existing [Constraint check] block: repeat value + count, product ids opened so far (max 4, deduped), which requested value is still unsatisfied on the current product page (reusing the incumbent's own matching helpers), and one concrete redirect naming the first product id visible on the most recent results page that has not been opened (else a one-keyword-change fallback). _strip_blocks/_with_blocks make re-injection idempotent for both blocks. transform_response stays identity; no state, no filesystem/network/subprocess, stdlib re/json/copy/ast only. Offline replay over all turns of all 50 candidate_01 + 50 baseline episodes: 0 exceptions, 0 firings on the 19 passing tasks (321,341,488,885,720,872,1006,718,691,444,230,232,654,304,684,417,961,820,874), 0 silent-turn output differences vs constraint_ledger, firing turns (54 total) confined to 9 failing episodes 251(10),329(8),425(1),465(14),680(7),827(10),300(1),787(1),801(2).
candidate.expected_efficiency: +~60-80 tokens on each of the 54 firing turns (~+4K tokens total worst case, no extra model calls, no effect on non-firing turns which are byte-identical to the incumbent). Expected net token reduction of 100K-250K if 2+ turn-cap loops short-circuit, since those 6 episodes alone spent 604K tokens (58.5% of all tokens) and 120 turns; turns drop only on converted or short-circuited loops. Prediction: 19/50 -> 21-23/50 (0.42-0.46); bounded downside on this batch because no passing episode ever repeats a click value, so the guard cannot alter any currently passing trajectory.

candidate.name: variant_code_check
candidate.hypothesis: A stateless '[Variant check]' line that fires only when the budget-stripped instruction carries a digit-bearing identifier (decimal, alphanumeric variant code, shade number, dimension mark; bare integers and '<count>-<package word>' quantity expressions excluded) and the current product page offers a not-yet-clicked option carrying every such identifier, will convert at least 2 of the 3 failing tasks where the required variant was visible but unclicked (223: '225zf-4', 300: '2'3" x 12'', 383: '3.38 fl oz') and lift the 50-task train pass rate from 20/50 (0.40) to >=22/50, without touching the other 47 tasks: replaying all 852 recorded model calls across the three evidence phases shows the block fires only on those 3 tasks and is byte-identical to the incumbent on every non-firing turn, including all 20 currently passing tasks.
candidate.changes: agents/variant_code_check.py = full copy of the incumbent agents/progress_guard.py (constraint ledger + repetition-triggered progress block, untouched) plus one transform_request-only mechanism. New helpers: an ordered identifier extractor over the budget-stripped instruction (shade codes, feet+inches, inch/foot marks, decimals, alphanumeric codes such as '225zf-4'/'3x-large'; bare integers and package-count forms like '2-pack' are dropped), a boundary-safe clickable tokenizer that keeps hyphens/quotes/periods inside tokens, and whole-token-or-prefix identifier matching. The block fires only when the latest observation is a product page (Price marker and clickables, no results-list marker), some offered option carries every extracted identifier, that option is not yet clicked, and no clicked option on the page carries the full identifier set; it then appends one line — 'Variant check: your instruction specifies <ids>; offered here as <option> — click it and verify before buying (no clicked option carries <ids>).' Non-firing requests are returned byte-identically to the incumbent. Injected text is re-injectable via the incumbent's _strip_blocks/_with_blocks markers. Stateless per call, stdlib re only, no task ids, no cross-episode state; transform_response stays identity.
candidate.expected_efficiency: +~35 tokens on each firing turn only (14 firing turns across all three phases, 3 of them in the incumbent's own run: 223 turn 3, 300 turns 12-14, 383 turn 3); zero token and zero turn change on every other turn (byte-identical requests); no extra model calls. Prediction: 20/50 (0.40) -> 22-23/50 (0.44-0.46) if 2-3 of 223/300/383 convert; token total roughly flat (<=+100 tokens on the incumbent's trajectories) with turns decreasing only if a converted episode stops re-searching.

candidate.name: joint_option_check
candidate.hypothesis: When the instruction requests two or more values that one offered option jointly satisfies, the incumbent's per-value '[Constraint check]' lines direct the solver to two or more conflicting click targets and the solver obeys both in sequence, buying a wrong variant; collapsing exactly those lines into one joint-option line (with a standalone-number guard so a requirement like '11' is never covered by an unrelated option such as 'a11') will convert at least one of the two provably misled failing episodes (674, 806) and lift the 50-task train pass rate from 21/50 (0.42) to >=22/50, while leaving all 21 passing episodes untouched: offline replay of all 315 recorded incumbent model calls shows the joint line fires on exactly 5 turns across 4 failing tasks (300 t3/t8, 674 t3, 806 t7, 868 t3) and the other 310 calls are byte-identical to the incumbent's output.
candidate.changes: agents/joint_option_check.py = full copy of the incumbent agents/variant_code_check.py plus one request-side mechanism (transform_request only; transform_response stays identity; no new block marker, joint line lives inside the existing [Constraint check] region; stateless, stdlib re/ast/copy/json only). Added helpers: _standalone_numbers(text) extracts numbers bounded by non-alphanumerics on both sides, and _jointly_covers(req, raw_value, groups) = incumbent _value_matches AND every standalone number of the requirement's raw text appears as a standalone number in the option. In _render_values bookkeeping, per-request actions are tracked; _joint_choice picks the offered option J* with maximum coverage, ties by fewest extra tokens then fewest tokens then lexicographic, and fires only when cov(J*) >= 2 and the covered values' per-value lines would otherwise direct >= 2 distinct click targets or mark one of them 'NOT offered'. On fire, those lines are removed and one line is inserted at the first removed position: "- <values>: all offered together as '<J*>' - click this one option." (or '- already clicked.' if J* was clicked page-locally). Budget line, buy gate, non-covered value lines, progress and variant blocks render exactly as the incumbent; non-firing calls are byte-identical to the incumbent output.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Fires on only 5 of 315 incumbent turns; each fire replaces 2-3 short lines with 1 line (~-40 prompt tokens per 50-task run), no extra model calls. Turns drop only if a converted episode stops clicking a conflicting option (806 may need one turn less). Prediction: 21/50 (0.42) -> 22-23/50 (0.44-0.46): 674 previously passed under the identity baseline with a click on the joint option and regressed only when the ledger's conflicting lines appeared; 806 is the second candidate conversion (the joint option string is offered verbatim). Verified offline: replay of all 1167 recorded calls across the four evidence phases shows 0 exceptions, 0 fires on any passing task in the three candidate phases, and byte-identity on every non-firing turn.

candidate.name: option_alignment_check
candidate.hypothesis: Retaining the incumbent variant_code_check ledger verbatim and adding two compact option-alignment arms inside the existing '[Constraint check]' block will convert batch-1 failures where a required option was visible on the page but never clicked: (1) rescued ledger lines re-try each value the incumbent would mark 'NOT offered' against the page's own option strings with whitespace-insensitive equality / prefix / suffix matching, token-boundary guarded, so a compact code like '3x' can land on an offered '3x-large' even though word tokenization splits it, and (2) one extra line surfaces an unclicked offered option whose label the instruction names verbatim when no rendered checklist/variant/progress line mentions it yet. Prediction: 13/50 (0.26) -> 15-16/50 if 1-3 of 204/318/786 convert, with zero changed calls on the 13 passing tasks and zero exceptions (offline replay of all 212 batch-1 model calls: 9 changed calls, all on the three intended failing tasks; 203 byte-identical; 0 calls changed on any passing task).
candidate.changes: New file agents/option_alignment_check.py = full copy of the incumbent agents/variant_code_check.py (constraint ledger, repetition-triggered progress block, digit-bearing variant check all untouched) plus one transform_request-only mechanism; transform_response stays identity; no new block marker, additions live inside the existing re-rendered '[Constraint check]' region so the incumbent strip/re-inject idempotency still applies. New helpers: _compact_form/_compact_match (lowercase + whitespace-crushed equality/prefix/suffix with a token-boundary guard; shorter side must be >=3 chars or exactly 2 chars with a digit, so a bare '3' cannot match, and non-boundary substring matches are refused), _requirement_forms (also tries the requested value with a leading generic attribute word stripped, e.g. 'size 3 x' -> '3 x'), _rescue_option (picks the best offered option), _option_is_clicked, _is_quantity_option, _label_span (verbatim contiguous token-run match, case/whitespace-insensitive, >=3 chars with a letter, word boundaries), _instruction_option_lines. Arm 1: in _render_values the final 'NOT offered' branch first tries _rescue_option and replaces the line with "- <raw>: offered as '<option>' - click it before buying." (or '- already clicked.' when the matched option is in the page-local clicked set); otherwise the original line renders byte-identically. Arm 2: on product pages only, offered options that are not nav/label controls, not clicked page-locally, not named anywhere in the rendered ledger/variant/progress text, and whose group (incumbent _value_groups) is inferred and outside _SURFACE_EXCLUDED_GROUPS (size, quantity, and the incumbent's _INCOMPATIBLE_COLOR_GROUPS) get one line "- <label>: your instruction names this option - click it before buying.", at most one per instruction span with the shortest matching label winning. The group gate is the tightening applied to keep passing tasks untouched: an initial non-size/non-quantity gate still let one flavor-group option fire on a passing task, so flavor/scent/style/pattern/theme/material were excluded too; after that, replay shows 0 changed calls on every passing task in both recorded batches. Stateless, stdlib re/ast/copy/json only, no task ids, no cross-episode state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Adds or rewrites lines only on firing turns: 9 of 212 recorded batch-1 calls change (6 Arm-1 rescue replacements that shorten an existing line, 3 Arm-2 surfacing lines of ~70 chars), net -54 characters (~-14 tokens) over the whole 212-call batch; worst case +~70 tokens per Arm-2 firing turn, 0 extra model calls, every other call byte-identical. The 315-call batch-0 sanity replay is 100% byte-identical (0 fires). Turn counts drop only if a converted episode stops re-searching/looping (the 20-turn size-code loop is the main candidate); otherwise tokens are flat to slightly negative.

candidate.name: option_group_title_anchor
candidate.hypothesis: Retaining the incumbent option_alignment_check ledger verbatim and appending at most one 'title-anchor' line inside the existing [Constraint check] region converts sample-1 failures where an offered option group was left at zero page-local clicks even though the product title names one of its values: the agent buys the correct-looking product without selecting the variant the title implies. The line fires only when a labeled offered group (a) has no clicked value on the current page, (b) shares no token with the instruction, and (c) contains an offered value whose tokens are a non-empty subset of the product title - so it is provably silent on every currently passing trajectory (0 fires on the 16 passing tasks; byte-identical output on all non-firing turns). Falsified if the sample-1 pass count does not increase or any passing task's trajectory changes.
candidate.changes: New file agents/option_group_title_anchor.py = full copy of the incumbent agents/option_alignment_check.py (constraint ledger, repetition-triggered progress block, digit-bearing variant check, and both option-alignment arms all untouched) plus one additive transform_request-only mechanism; transform_response stays identity; no new block marker, the line lives inside the already re-rendered [Constraint check] region so the incumbent strip/re-inject idempotency still applies. New helpers: _hint_tokens (lowercase alphanumeric tokens) and _title_anchor_line(instruction, content, offered, groups, clicked) -> str | None. Hook: in the is_product branch of _ledger_block, right after the _instruction_option_lines call, append '- <value>: the product title contains this option — click it before buying.' Deterministic iteration over _value_groups order; first qualifying group, first title-contained value; group-level instruction-disjointness (no token of any offered value in the group occurs in the instruction) is the tightening that keeps passing color groups (e.g. an instruction-named group) silent. Stateless, stdlib re/copy/json/ast only (imports unchanged), no task ids, no cross-episode state, no runtime I/O.
candidate.expected_efficiency: +1 line (~15-20 tokens) only on firing turns: offline replay of all 189 recorded sample-1 incumbent model calls shows 9 firing turns on 7 failing tasks (253 t3, 289 t3+t4, 429 t3, 441 t3, 473 t3, 529 t3+t4, 954 t3), 0 exceptions, 180/180 non-firing calls byte-identical, 0 fires on the 16 passing tasks; replay over the 50 identity-baseline sample-1 episodes used the same trigger. No extra model calls; turns change only if a converted episode stops re-searching. Prediction: 16/50 (0.32) -> 17-19/50 (0.34-0.38) if 1-3 of the 7 fired failures convert, with zero expected downside on the passing set.
